name: resync_pipeline
description: Resyncs the specified `pipeline_id` by running the historical load again for all of its active objects. Use the `drop_and_load` parameter to specify whether Hevo drops and recreates the Destination tables before it loads the historical data again. The request body is optional, and leaving it out is the same as setting `drop_and_load` to `false`. With `false`, Hevo keeps your Destination tables, applies any schema changes to them and loads the data into them again. When you resync a Pipeline, Hevo performs the following actions: - Deletes the schedules of the Pipeline and cancels the jobs that are running. - Releases the resources that Hevo created in your Source, such as the replication slot on a PostgreSQL Source. - Reads the Source schema and the Destination schema again, and resets the object mappings. - Restores the schedule of the Pipeline. If `schedule.sync_type` is `ON_DEMAND`, the sync starts immediately. If the resync fails, the Pipeline moves to the `Failed` state. Read Resync Pipeline for more information about the actions performed on your Pipeline when you resync it. The response returns the Pipeline in the `Restarting` state, and the Pipeline reaches the `Initialized` state once the action completes. To re-ingest particular objects without resyncing the whole Pipeline, use the [Trigger Resync for a Set of Objects](/reference/post_api-v2-pipelines-pipeline-id-objects-actions-resync) endpoint instead. Refer to [Resyncing a Pipeline](/reference/syncing-and-resyncing-pipelines#resyncing-a-pipeline) for more information about when and how to resync a Pipeline.
consequence: Reloads all the data from the Source. If the request asks to re-create the tables, the tables in the Destination are deleted and created again.
title: Resync Edge Pipeline

drop_and_load.description: If set to true, Hevo drops and recreates the Destination tables for all active objects. Data from the Source objects is then re-ingested and loaded into the newly created Destination tables.

code.description: Status of the API call. Returns `Accepted` when the request is accepted.

message.description: Description of the action that Hevo performed.

state.description:
Current lifecycle state of the Pipeline.

This endpoint never returns `Deleting` or `Deleted`.

x-enumDescriptions.Created: Pipeline has been created, but the full configuration is still in progress.
x-enumDescriptions.Created Source: Source has been configured for the Pipeline.
x-enumDescriptions.Created Destination: Destination has been configured for the Pipeline.
x-enumDescriptions.Configured Object: Objects have been configured for replication.
x-enumDescriptions.Initializing: Pipeline is starting and preparing to replicate data.
x-enumDescriptions.Initialized: Pipeline has been fully set up and is replicating data.
x-enumDescriptions.Disabled: Pipeline has been disabled and is no longer replicating data.
x-enumDescriptions.Restarting: Pipeline is restarting after a resync.
x-enumDescriptions.Failed: Pipeline could not be set up or could not continue replicating data.

disabled.description: Indicates whether the Pipeline is disabled. This value is _true_ while the Pipeline is in the _Disabled_ or _Disabling_ state. This value is `false` while the Pipeline is in the _Enabling_ state.

health.description: Condition of the Pipeline's runs, as the Pipeline Overview in the Hevo UI shows it. Hevo returns this object for a single Pipeline only, in the response of a read or an action, and omits it from a list of Pipelines and when it cannot access job monitoring. It is also left out when Hevo has no label for the health state it reads.

x-enumDescriptions.HEALTHY: The last run completed and nothing needs attention.
x-enumDescriptions.NEEDS_ATTENTION: The last run failed and the Pipeline needs attention.
x-enumDescriptions.DEFERRED: A run is holding until it can proceed.
x-enumDescriptions.HISTORICAL_RUN_IN_PROGRESS: A historical load is in progress.

display_name.description: The label the Hevo UI shows for this condition. For example, _Healthy_.

severity.description: Severity level that the Hevo UI uses to show this condition. For example, _success_.

source.description: Source details configured in the Pipeline.

name.description: Name specified for the Source in Hevo.

connector_id.description: Identifier of the connector that ingests data from this Source. This is the `connector_id` value that the Pipeline was created with. For example, _SOURCE_CONNECTOR_POSTGRES_.

destination_id.description: Unique identifier of the Destination the Pipeline loads into.

destination.description: Destination details configured in the Pipeline.

name.description: Name specified for the Destination in Hevo.

connector_id.description: Identifier of the connector used to load data into this Destination.

status.description:
Current status of the Destination.

This endpoint never returns `DELETING`, `DELETED` or `DELETE_FAILED`.

x-enumDescriptions.CREATED: The Destination is ready to receive data.
x-enumDescriptions.FAILED: Hevo created the Destination but could not complete its setup.

destination_prefix.description: Prefix used for Destination table names.

load_mode.description: Mode used to load data from the Source objects into the Destination tables.

x-enumDescriptions.APPEND: New records are added at the end of your Destination table without modifying or deleting any existing data.
x-enumDescriptions.MERGE: Existing records are updated based on matching criteria, such as primary keys, and new records are added to your Destination table if no match is found.
x-enumDescriptions.OVERWRITE: Each load replaces all the records in your Destination table. You cannot set it while creating or modifying a Pipeline, and a Pipeline that uses it can be switched to another load mode.

schema_evolution.description: Policy for applying Source schema changes to the Destination schema.

x-enumDescriptions.ALLOW_ALL: Hevo replicates all Source schema changes, such as new or updated columns and tables, to the Destination.
x-enumDescriptions.BLOCK_ALL: Hevo does not replicate any Source schema changes to the Destination.
x-enumDescriptions.ALLOW_COLUMN_LEVEL: Hevo replicates only new columns from the Source to the Destination. New schemas and tables are not synced.

replication_type.description: Type of data Hevo replicates from your Source objects.

x-enumDescriptions.HISTORICAL_AND_INCREMENTAL: Hevo first replicates all existing data from the selected Source objects and then captures only data changes.
x-enumDescriptions.INCREMENTAL_ONLY: Hevo replicates only new and changed data from your Source object after the Pipeline is created.

sync_type.description: Determines how Pipeline runs are triggered.

x-enumDescriptions.SCHEDULED: Pipeline runs automatically at the interval set in frequency_minutes.
x-enumDescriptions.ON_DEMAND: Pipeline runs only when you trigger it. Hevo does not run it automatically.

frequency_minutes.description: Interval between Pipeline runs (in minutes). This field is always present. Its value is `null` when the Pipeline has no fixed interval. Ignore this value when `sync_type` is `ON_DEMAND`.

schedule.description: Interval at which the Pipeline runs jobs to process data.

enabled.description: Indicates whether alerts are enabled for Pipeline latency.

threshold_minutes.description: Delay after which Hevo sends you a latency alert (in minutes). Hevo measures this delay from the time your data is ready in the Source to the time it is loaded into your Destination. This field is always present. Its value is `null` when `enabled` is `false`, and also when the alert is on but no threshold is stored.

latency_alert.description: Configuration for triggering alerts when data loading is delayed.

object_failure_level.description: Handling of data replication if an object fails.

x-enumDescriptions.PARTIAL: If an object fails, the Pipeline continues replicating data for the remaining objects.
x-enumDescriptions.ALL_OR_NONE: Hevo loads the data of an object only when all of its Events are processed successfully in a job.

object_failure_threshold.description: Number of failed Events allowed for an object in a job. Hevo stops loading the data of that object once its failed Events exceed this number. This value applies only when `object_failure_level` is `PARTIAL`. The field is always present, and its value can be `null` for a Pipeline that does not store one, such as one set to `ALL_OR_NONE`.

failure_handling_policy.description: Defines how failures are handled for Source objects.

source_schema_status.description: Details of the Source schema for this Pipeline.

status.description: Current status of the Source schema.

x-enumDescriptions.REQUESTED: Hevo is reading the schema of your Source.
x-enumDescriptions.COMPLETED: Hevo has read the schema of your Source, and the object list is ready.
x-enumDescriptions.FAILED: Hevo could not read the schema of your Source.

refreshed_at.description: Timestamp when the Source schema was last refreshed, in Unix epoch time (in milliseconds). This value is `null` until Hevo refreshes the schema for the first time.

runs.description: Details of the last Pipeline run, the next scheduled run, and any run currently in progress. When this object is returned, all four of its keys (`last_completed`, `active`, `next_run` and `last_seven_days`) are present, and a key with no value is `null`. Hevo leaves out `runs` and `health` together when it cannot read the job overview, and leaves out `source_schema_status` when it cannot read the Source schema.

job_id.description: Unique identifier of the job. Hevo returns this field in the `runs.last_completed` object and in each object of the `runs.active` array.

type.description: Type of job, such as a historical load, an incremental run or a data refresher run.

status.description: Current status of the job. The values are the same as the ones the job endpoints return, including `CANCELED` and `CANCELING`.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the job was created, in Unix epoch time (in milliseconds).

active.description: Jobs that are running for the Pipeline right now. This list is empty when no job is running.

job_id.description: Unique identifier of the job. Hevo returns this field in the `runs.last_completed` object and in each object of the `runs.active` array.

type.description: Type of job, such as a historical load, an incremental run or a data refresher run.

status.description: Current status of the job. The values are the same as the ones the job endpoints return, including `CANCELED` and `CANCELING`.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the job was created, in Unix epoch time (in milliseconds).

next_run.description: Time at which Hevo expects the Pipeline to run next. This value is `null` when Hevo cannot determine the next run.

kind.description: Condition on which the time of the next run is set. This value is `AT_TIME` when Hevo has estimated the start time of the next run and returns it in the `at` field, and `ON_SCHEDULE` when the Pipeline runs on a custom schedule, for which `at` is `null`.

at.description: Timestamp of the next run, in Unix epoch time (in milliseconds), or `null`.

last_seven_days.description: Events that the Pipeline processed in the last seven days, split into `historical`, `incremental` and `refresher`.

ingested.description: Number of Events read from the Source. This count can be lower than the number of loaded Events.

loaded.description: Number of Events loaded into the Destination.

failed.description: Number of Events that could not be processed.

ingested.description: Number of Events read from the Source. This count can be lower than the number of loaded Events.

loaded.description: Number of Events loaded into the Destination.

failed.description: Number of Events that could not be processed.

ingested.description: Number of Events read from the Source. This count can be lower than the number of loaded Events.

loaded.description: Number of Events loaded into the Destination.

failed.description: Number of Events that could not be processed.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the Pipeline was created, in Unix epoch time (in milliseconds).

created_by.description: Email address of the user who created the Pipeline.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the Pipeline was last updated, in Unix epoch time (in milliseconds).

updated_by.description: Email address of the user who last updated the Pipeline.
